points.description: The answer conveys that in asynchronous transmission each character is sent on its own as a self-contained unit framed by a start bit and a stop bit, which is simple and cheap but gives lower transmission rates.

The answer conveys that in synchronous transmission characters are grouped into a continuous stream of frames delimited by a SYN or flag pattern, which is more complex, needs sender and receiver to stay synchronized, and gives higher transmission rates.

rubric.notes: The question is a single short comparison worth 1 mark, so the scheme has two points, one for each mode. Full marks require the student to describe the defining feature of each mode (per-character start/stop framing for asynchronous; continuous frames with SYN/flag and synchronization for synchronous). Equivalent wording, and the rate or complexity trade-off stated in plain words, is accepted. A student who describes only one mode, or who only lists features without the core distinction, earns no mark for the missing mode.
